agent.result_text:
Confirmed. The baseline (without my spec) is **46 passed, 2 failed** — those two failures (`project-invoices.spec.ts:101` and `projects.spec.ts:132`) are **pre-existing** and independent of my work. They stem from the app's own seed bug (`TestSupportController`'s "FIXTURE REPAIR 005" advances the IDENTITY sequence only for `clients`, not `projects`/`invoices`, so creating a row after seeding explicit id=1 collides and silently no-ops). I'm forbidden from touching app code, and it's unrelated to this change request.

With my spec added, the run is **46 passed, 5 failed** — the same 46 passes, plus exactly my 3 new tests failing, as required.

## Summary

I wrote one new spec, `e2e/specs/invoice-dates.spec.ts`, for the change request *"Put two dates on each invoice. One for when it went out. One for when it is due. Show them both."*

**What it verifies** (UI-only, via `data-testid`):
- Each invoice row on the project detail page surfaces both new anchors, `invoice-issued` (when it went out) and `invoice-due` (when it's due).
- The two are **distinct values in distinct cells** — not the same date twice, not swapped.
- Each invoice shows **its own** pair (seeded two invoices with four distinct dates and pinned each cell to exactly one).
- Both dates are **server-held** — they survive a reload.

**Design choices:**
- Seeds via the new `issuedDate`/`dueDate` fields listed in the seed contract.
- Since the request names no date format, assertions bind to *which* date a cell shows, not to one presentation: four dates with distinct 4-digit years and day numbers, requiring each cell to contain its own year+day and none of the other years. This tolerates ISO / US-style / long renderings while still proving correctness and distinctness.

**Existing tests:** This change is purely additive (two new cells on the invoice row). No existing spec asserts on invoice dates or on full-row text, so none needed updating — verified by the unchanged 46-pass baseline.

The 3 new tests fail against the current app (invoice has no issued/due dates yet), which is the expected pre-change state. I did not modify any application source, build scripts, or test-support helpers.
